findings.issue_text: EventManager calls updateEvent with an undefined credential when a calendar reference credentialId is missing from both in-memory credentials and the database, causing booking updates/reschedules to throw.

CalendarService.updateEvent has an inverted fallback destination-calendar lookup: when externalCalendarId is absent, it compares externalId to an absent value and fails to select the configured destination calendar.
CalendarService.deleteEvent has the same inverted fallback destination-calendar lookup, so deletes without externalCalendarId can use the default calendar instead of the configured destination.
handleNewBooking persists only the first destination calendar for collective bookings, losing other host destination calendars needed by later cancellation, confirmation, payment, and reminder flows.

goldens.comment: A null reference occurs in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() and updateEvent() when mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar but evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, causing mainHostDestinationCalendar to be undefined.
The optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant since you already check mainHostDestinationCalendar in the ternary condition.

Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.

Logic inversion in organization creation: The slug property is now conditionally set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, instead of when it's false as originally intended. This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled

The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only—this breaks the interface contract (also applies to other locations in the PR).

The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CalendarService.updateEvent has an inverted fallback destination-calendar lookup: when externalCalendarId is absent, it compares externalId to an absent value and fails to select the configured destination calendar.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff in GoogleCalendarService.ts, the updateEvent method has this code: `const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. When externalCalendarId is falsy (the else branch), it tries to find a calendar where `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId`, but externalCalendarId is undefined/null at that point, so this will never match any calendar. The same bug exists in deleteEvent. This is a real logic error - the fallback should likely use a different criteria (like credentialId) or just take the first destination calendar, not compare against the undefined externalCalendarId.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CalendarService.deleteEvent has the same inverted fallback destination-calendar lookup, so deletes without externalCalendarId can use the default calendar instead of the configured destination.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for GoogleCalendarService.deleteEvent (lines 312-318), the code shows: `const calendarId = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. This is indeed a logical error - when externalCalendarId is falsy (the else branch), the code tries to find a calendar where `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId`, but externalCalendarId is undefined/null at that point, so this will never match anything and will always return undefined. This means deletes without an externalCalendarId will fall back to 'primary' calendar instead of using the configured destination calendar. This is the same bug pattern as in updateEvent.

adjudication_records.issue_text: handleNewBooking persists only the first destination calendar for collective bookings, losing other host destination calendars needed by later cancellation, confirmation, payment, and reminder flows.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows changes to support multiple destination calendars (changing from single DestinationCalendar to DestinationCalendar[] array). The finding claims handleNewBooking only persists the first destination calendar, but handleNewBooking.ts is not included in this diff. The diff shows EventManager.ts, CalendarManager.ts, and various calendar services being updated to handle arrays of destination calendars. Without seeing handleNewBooking.ts in the diff, I cannot verify this claim. The finding is speculating about code not shown in the diff.
